cohorts.comparison: Prioritize Good Samaritan Atlanta, Mosaic Health, Ethne, Healing Bridge, Lions Lighthouse, CBWW and CPACS for relatively legible underserved-access or specialty pathways. Urban Clinic, Good Sam Gwinnett and Coweta/Willing Helpers/Bethesda are strong reserves, not weaker-effectiveness findings. Mercy and Grady have especially important safety-net work but affiliated/leveraged full-cost and payer accounting is less immediately tractable. GTF tests medication/financial access but transfers need clinical follow-through. GHFA grants and Friends of Refugees maternal support remain meaningful alternatives; count grantee/clinical partner costs. CPACS broad portfolio is retained for differentiated language-access reach, not treated as a clinic-only gift.
cohorts.falsifier: Other providers, public insurance, screening harms, low adherence and donated-resource costs may erase gains.

cohorts.comparison: Positive Impact is prioritized for integrated delivered HIV care and clear metro clinics. SisterLove and NAESM are differentiated community-access reserves; AID Atlanta is a credible clinical comparator, but AHF affiliation and public/pharmacy funding complicate the ordinary margin. No recipient is credited merely for tests, contacts or historical HIV burden.
cohorts.falsifier: Testing is not infection prevention; Ryan White, pharmacy revenues and alternate HIV providers may fully substitute.

cohorts.comparison: Georgia Harm Reduction Coalition is prioritized for a concrete high-risk delivery pathway; Georgia Council for Recovery is a valuable peer/advocacy comparator with a longer causal chain. Prefer resolving actual additional naloxone/safer-use/clinical linkage over importing a generic per-kit life-saved rate. Preserve possible zero or adverse effects.
cohorts.falsifier: No one reversal equals one life; public naloxone, substitution, finite survival, competing mortality and actual treatment retention matter.

cohorts.comparison: CHRIS180 and Odyssey are prioritized for delivered youth/adult therapy, with Summit and Link close reduced-fee alternatives. GMHCN offers a distinct respite/peer route; MHA and NAMI emphasize education/support rather than assumed treatment. Skyland/Hillside residential care can be valuable but full costs, national origins and counterfactual treatment make first-pass pricing harder. Families First, Kate’s Club, Ser Familia and RWN are retained for differentiated populations, not discounted solely for being broad; clinical conversion of peer/family support remains uncertain.
cohorts.falsifier: Sessions, peer contacts and training do not establish net utility; usual care, dropout, recurrence and treatment harm must be modeled.

cohorts.comparison: ARC-Southeast offers an explicit financial/logistical access mechanism; HMHBGA tests statewide perinatal navigation and policy leverage. Feminist Center is the nearest direct-clinical reserve, while SisterSong adds national organizing/birth-justice work. Legal restrictions, geography and alternative funds are essential; no assumption that every funded procedure changes health or that public reimbursement is unchanged.
cohorts.falsifier: Care may occur anyway through other funds; eligibility, legal timing, maternal outcomes and harms require intervention-specific evidence.

cohorts.comparison: Prioritize AVLF and Atlanta Legal Aid for direct housing/safety cases, GHF for coverage access/policy, and Georgia Appleseed for healthy housing/child supports. Georgia Watch/GBPI are strong policy reserves. GLSP extends to outer metro counties rather than duplicating Atlanta Legal Aid; GAO provides disability protection, GJP/SCHR/Women on the Rise justice pathways and LAA immigration/basic-needs access. Their legal/policy achievements remain potentially valuable but are not health units; reject automatic coalition-wide credit.
cohorts.falsifier: Case wins, coverage, debt relief and legislation are not QALYs; causality, alternate counsel, implementation and overlapping coalitions matter.

cohorts.comparison: Mosaic Georgia and Raksha are prioritized for clinically proximate trauma services and differentiated access. PADV, In Safe Company and LiveSafe are close broad survivor reserves; Cherokee, Promise Place, Haven House, IWH and Tapestri diversify catchments and populations. Tapestri is not shelter. GCCA and youthSpark add child intervention/prevention. Selection is research information value, not a claim one survivor population is more deserving or agency effectiveness is measured.
cohorts.falsifier: Shelter, forensic exams and advocacy do not directly measure reduced violence; public grants, substitution and adverse responses matter.

cohorts.comparison: Propel ATL has a tightly local injury/active-transport mechanism; Mothers and Others for Clean Air has explicit child exposure interventions. GCV Education Fund, PSE, Southface and GIPL offer potentially scalable policy/building leverage but wider attribution/resource burdens. Live Thrive and Chattahoochee Riverkeeper have tangible waste/water work, yet volume monitoring is farther from a measured health effect. All comparisons preserve public substitution, climate/nonlocal effects and displacement harms.
cohorts.falsifier: Policy wins, recycled weight and equipment counts are not health gains; timing, public finance, coalition credit and displaced risks matter.

cohorts.comparison: HOPE Atlanta and Our House are prioritized for prevention/stabilization and integrated family health, with Status: Home for the housing/HIV pathway. CAC, Nicholas House, CaringWorks, Lost-n-Found, Covenant House, Drake and Family Promise are strong differentiated reserves. Gateway/Atlanta Mission/MUST offer broader bundles, Housing Plus rent assistance, SVdP local-conference support, Giving Kitchen national worker crises, New American Pathways refugee integration, and GAEH/Partners for HOME coordination. No automatic shelter-night or rent-dollar health value; avoid duplicating food, healthcare and grant partners.
cohorts.falsifier: Housing transfers, capital assets, public subsidies, alternative shelter and overlapping care can dominate marginal benefit.

cohorts.comparison: Open Hand is prioritized for illness-tailored nutrition, with Meals On Wheels as a senior nutrition/home-repair comparator. ACFB, Second Helpings, Concrete Jungle and Sweetwater have concrete food-access routes; Feeding Georgia adds policy/coordination. Food rescue, banking and downstream pantry delivery cannot each receive all benefit. Clinical nutrition contracts and substitution still matter, and no observational healthcare-cost saving is adopted as causal.
cohorts.falsifier: Food volumes, recovered value and uncontrolled medical-cost associations are not causal health outcomes; source and downstream delivery overlap.

comparisonCaveat: Research priorities are explicit judgment, not numerical cost-effectiveness ranks or donor endorsements. A valid finite judgment alpha estimate can survive missing observed marginal parameters; discovery does not establish those estimates.
